targets.label_en: Provides a list of previously saved interactive sessions
Resumes the most recently ended session

6.explanation_en:
copilot --resume opens a picker that lists previously saved interactive sessions so you can choose one to resume.
copilot --continue resumes the most recently ended session directly, without showing the list.
--add-dir grants access to an extra directory, --model selects the model, and --prompt runs a single prompt non-interactively.

15.explanation_en:
Box 1: gh extension install github/copilot (official answer in the source).
Box 2: copilot — running the copilot command with no arguments starts an interactive session. /new and /session are slash commands used inside an already running session.
Note: the current standalone GitHub Copilot CLI is also installed with npm install -g @github/copilot (or winget). The source's answer image marks the gh extension option, so that is what is scored here.

sources_en: Open a browser-based GitHub sign-in flow.

targets.correct_en: Open a browser-based GitHub sign-in flow.

82.explanation_en:
1. Run gh auth login to authenticate the GitHub CLI.
2. Complete the browser-based GitHub sign-in flow.
3. Confirm folder trust so Copilot may read and modify files in the project folder.
4. Run copilot from the project root to start the interactive session.
/login is used inside an already running session, and copilot --resume resumes a previous session rather than starting a new one.

128.explanation_en:
Inside a running Copilot CLI session, the /add-dir slash command adds a trusted directory so Copilot can read and modify its files, without restarting the CLI.
The argument is the plain path /repo/tests. The @ prefix is used to mention a file as context in a prompt, not to grant directory access.
(The source image lists /repo/tests twice in the second dropdown; the duplicate is merged here.)
